[2024-03-17T23:42:51.000Z] [id:c17e792c-65d8-4c8c-93c3-574373d3c3c1] [lang:en] ADVANCED BERRI RATING POST 1

[2024-03-17T23:45:02.000Z] [id:92f36361-8356-423c-9c3e-1d383f8ccaf4] [lang:en] ADVANCED BERRI RATING POST 2
The Advanced Berri Rating essentially measures how effective a team is at producing box score statistics that correlate with wins according to the academic research of Professor David Berri, as set forth in his book @mention
[2024-03-17T23:47:06.000Z] [id:bc880acb-b7ad-4dd2-8c96-8730d966091d] [lang:en] ADVANCED BERRI RATING POST 3
Effectively, the first layer is called the "Berri Rating" and it is a measurement of a team's ability to produce the box score stats that produce wins COMPARED to the team's opponents average YIELD of such statistics.
[2024-03-17T23:49:27.000Z] [id:2edeb613-9e0e-41a1-8fe1-fb3ff36d3c41] [lang:en] ADVANCED BERRI RATING POST 4
But in college, some teams play "The Little Sisters of the Poor". So, unlike in the NBA, we have to go one more level to effectively measure the strength of the team's schedule by measuring ITS Berri Rating
[2024-03-17T23:50:51.000Z] [id:22018d25-20cb-488b-af05-76f0c9eb9042] [lang:en] ADVANCED BERRI RATING Post 5
So, an Advanced Berri Rating also asks what the Average Berri Rating is of each team's opponents. The higher that rate the tougher their schedule. So that is then added to the Team's Berri Rating to produce the Advanced Berri Rating.
[2024-03-17T23:52:46.000Z] [id:5d7925ea-74e1-4642-9331-9fe99ac48a97] [lang:en] ADVANCED BERRI RATING Post 6
In that sense, the Advanced Berri Rating is modeled after the classic NCAA RPI. However, where the RPI is arbitrary (why count "Opponents's Opponents" only 25%?) the Advanced Berri Rating is logically sound and the best method available
